proposals.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich halide with no Zr, La, P, B or Si. Its F- anion is much less prone than phosphate, borate or silicate anions to displacing La or Zr from LLZO, so it should avoid the LaPO4/ZrO2 and LaBO3 contact products that have set the penalty for every oxide coating so far. It is also chemically inert toward LiCoO2 near 4 V and in a family not yet tested.

proposals.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap (about 5 eV), electronically insulating, binary Li-rich oxide with no Zr, La, P, B or Si. Its very high Li2O content matches the Li-rich character of LLZO, so it should not offer a driving force to displace La or Zr, unlike the phosphate, borate, silicate and LiF coatings tested so far. It is also chemically inert toward LiCoO2 near 4 V, and its composition is the most Li-rich available.
proposals.motivation: Every evaluated coating so far failed the 0.05 eV limit, mostly through La/Zr displacement at the LLZO side (best was about 0.099 for Li6Si2O7, bin 4). The Li-rich silicate line has plateaued, and LiF (a different family) was worse at 0.126. Li2O is the most Li2O-rich member of the available set and a chemically distinct binary oxide.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV), electronically insulating, Li-rich phosphate. It is chemically compatible with both LLZO (no new Zr/La reactions expected) and LiCoO2 (no transition-metal interdiffusion). Its phosphate framework should resist oxidation near 4 V and reduction at the Li-rich interface, so it is a plausible low-penalty interphase.

Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich zirconate. Its Zr(IV) matches the Zr already in LLZO, so the coating should avoid new Zr/La exchange at the LLZO interface, unlike the phosphate, which formed LaPO4 and ZrO2. Its Li2O-rich oxide framework should also be chemically tolerant toward LiCoO2 near 4 V.

It should avoid the La/Zr displacement reactions seen with Li3PO4 and Li2ZrO3, and it is in a new family to test a lower contact penalty.
